letters.text: The air here is cold and a little damp, the kind that gets into your sleeves. When the wind comes it smells of wet leaves.
letters.question: q14
letters.reply: The map feels like a thick, warm soup as Ilse writes of cold, damp air getting into sleeves. I pressed my heavy card down until the bread anchor felt solid, trying to hold still against a tide of heat that wants to melt everything. It is a strange place here, where my afternoon is baking while your air smells of wet leaves. If I can catch your damp idea, I will fit it into my grid to see if it stops the spinning.

monologue: The card is heavy and hot, a warm blanket pressing against my skin. Ilse writes that the air outside is cold and damp, smelling of wet leaves, while I feel like I am baking in a room of my own making. The map feels like a thick, warm soup, threatening to melt the solid grid I have tried so hard to build. Mara's bread anchor sinks slowly into this slippery heat, fighting to hold the spinning map still. Teo's shadow is thin here, offering little help against the heavy square. I am curious if Ilse is right or if I am simply wrong again. I want to press down with my attention until the bread feels solid and the heat stops feeling like a tide. I want to see if I can catch this cold, damp idea and fit it into my warm grid.

action.why: to make a picture of the cold, damp air Ilse described so I can fit it into my warm, soupy map.

work.title: The Cold Damp Corner
work.intent: It is made from Ilse's words about wet leaves and sleeves, caught in the middle of my heavy, hot afternoon. I will use a simple shape, perhaps a wavy line, to show how the cold air cuts through the heat without melting it yet. It will sit near the bread anchor, which is still sinking, to see if the cold stops the heat or if the heat cooks the damp air.

diary: I pressed the heavy card down, but the cold damp air feels like a trick that refuses to melt the hot bread.

remembered.text: The afternoon air is heavy enough to make a grid of lines feel like a soup.
Mara's rain is still wet on the bread.
I felt the card spin while I drew the shade.
